company_notes:
Client: Verdant Commons AI — healthcare platform (clinician-facing chat + records search). PHI in scope -> high compliance bar. Quick bullets/summary below:

- Use cases: clinician support chat, real-time summarization of notes, embeddings for record retrieval, reranking for diagnosis suggestions.
- Perf targets surfaced in SE calls: p95 latency target ~50-75ms for chat in steady state; allow tail up to ~200ms under load. Embeddings throughput target 150-250 req/s per region during peak.
- Dedicated sizing: SE recommended initial reserved pool = 8 x A100-equivalent (us-east + us-west), autoscale + burst policy to 16 for seasonal peaks. Client wants explicit reserved GPU counts per region in contract.
- SLA/throughput asks: procurement wants 99.95% uptime + latency SLOs with financial credits for breaches. Big ask: credits must materially cover multi-hour outage (legal wants >=50% ARR credit for >=2hr outage). Redwood standard credit bands flagged as insufficient.
- Procurement/security blockers: DPA/MSA redlines around data processing terms, breach notification timing (48-72 hr), indemnity clause, and required change to liability cap. Insurance: client requires cyber liability endorsement of $20M; Redwood standard doc cites $5M — procurement pushing for endorsement or certificate.
- Compliance asks: SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 cert, penetration test summary, vuln remediation SLA, KMS/HSM support for key custody, audit logging with 7-year retention, and US-only data residency.
- On-prem & VPC: Customer exploring Private (VPC) as primary; on-prem package requested as fallback for regulatory workloads. Pricing delta and packaging details will be part of procurement appendix.
- POC plan: 2-week Dedicated perf run in us-east with representative PHI-like dataset (anonymized). Performance goals to be validated against target throughput/latency, KV cache hit rates, and cold-start behavior under scaled burst. SE to provide perf script + load profile.
- Quotes from calls: "We cannot accept SLA credits that are purely token-based; need real financial indemnity for patient-impacting outages." — Head of Procurement. "Security will not sign MSA without SOC2 artifacts and explicit KMS support." — CISO.
- Competitive positioning: client is running parallel eval with OctaveAI and one hyperscaler-managed endpoint. Decision drivers: latency SLO guarantees, contract language on credits/liability, ease of private/on-prem deployment, and security evidence.
- Short-term asks for Redwood: 1) Provide SOC2 Type II + ISO docs and PT summary; 2) Draft of Dedicated-specific SLA appendix with explicit reserved GPU counts and maintenance windows, 3) Confirm cyber insurance limits / carrier endorsement options, 4) Provide template DPA with proposed redline responses for indemnity and notification timelines, 5) Schedule Dedicated perf POC week (preferred window: 2026-03-22 to 2026-03-29).
- Internal owner notes: AE (Avery) to drive legal intro; SE (Riley) to flesh out perf scripts; Security (Jordan) to prep artifacts. Procurement timeline: aiming for signed MSA + DPA by 2026-05 if blockers resolved.

Next steps (short): legal to review/redline DPA, set SLA negotiation call (procurement + pricing), lock POC date, confirm insurance paperwork.
